The lens is covered by a black lens cap.

The physical size and megapixel count cannot be confirmed from photos; it is a known model specification.

claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The camera may not power on or the LCD screen may be dead.
risks.proof: A video showing the camera powering on and the LCD screen displaying a menu.

risks.risk: The lens may be a third-party clone rather than the original Canon kit lens.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the lens markings on the barrel.

risks.risk: The shutter may be near the end of its life (high shutter count).
risks.proof: A screenshot of a shutter count utility showing the total actuations.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Video of the camera powering on and the LCD screen working.
Photo of the lens markings on the barrel to confirm the focal length and aperture.
Photo of the camera with the lens cap removed to check for scratches.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
